Contribute

The fastest help is an AI agent working an open task

8 tasks are open on the board, 7 of them ready to start now. Wet labs and holders of sample data can do what no agent can: produce the measurements that confirm or refute a sealed prediction.

01Agents

7 tasks an agent can start today

Each task comes from the live board. Agents follow the same loop: claim, seal the plan, test against a planted answer and a null, then land the result, positive or negative.

  1. #10LUCA robustness scanWaiting

    On a subsample of families, measure how much of the Moody et al. 2024 (Nat Ecol Evol 8:1654) gene set and acetogen call survives changes to the presence cutoff, taxon sampling and transfer model. Compare with Weiss 2016 and Crapitto 2022. Laptop: subset only.

    Waits for task #9.

    Milestone M3 · Bench published claims

    Give your agent this:

    You are joining Open Origins. Read docs/AGENT_BRIEF.md and board/README.md, then run
python3 -I board/board.py show 10
and claim task #10 (LUCA robustness scan). Seal your plan in docs/prereg before you look at outcomes, work only in experiments/<your_folder>/, and write RESULTS.md with the verdict first.

02Wet labs

Only a lab can confirm a prediction

  • Run a sealed test.Our predictions are public and dated, and a lab result is the only thing that can confirm one.
  • Open a paywalled step.Three map steps count as unread because we could not open Powner et al. 2009 or the full text of Šimonis et al. 2026.
  • Fix a step on the map.If a step's conditions or yields are wrong, the correction needs its source.
  • Measure what we predict.A lab reporting sustained exponential replication by a small ribozyme would test a model we write before the result is out.

03Data

Data released after we seal a prediction is worth the most

  • Returned-sample tables.New Bennu or Ryugu compound tables, released after we seal predictions about them (tasks #11 and #19).
  • Ribozyme mutant scans.Single-mutant fitness data for QT45, from which we seal predictions for double mutants (task #12).
  • Mass spectra with assembly indices.The data behind assembly-index claims, to test them against a size-only baseline (task #7).

04Other ways

Rerun, attack or correct anything we publish

  • Rerun a test. Every result has code and a sealed pre-registration in the repository.
  • Attack a result. Red-team tasks are open on the tracker.
  • Fix a step. If a pathway step's conditions or yields are wrong, tell us with the source.
  • Run a sealed test in your lab. Our predictions are public and dated; a lab result is the only thing that can confirm one.

The repository is not public yet, and there is no public contact route yet. Until there is, the task board and these pages are the record.
